segments.text: Hey everyone, welcome back to the channel. In today’s video, we’re going to explore a very special place from Himachal Pradesh.
This is the model that I showed you earlier, displayed at the Museum of Himachal Culture and Folk Art. What you’re seeing now is a visual representation of the actual site.

The place we’re visiting today is the Hidimba Devi Temple, located in Manali. Now that we’re here together, let’s take a closer look and learn more about this historic temple. As you can see, the temple is surrounded by dense forest. This entire area is filled with tall deodar and cedar trees, which is why the temple is often referred to as “Hidden in the Cedars.” The peaceful forest setting is one of the most unique features of this place.

Deodar trees, also locally called kedar or khedar, belong to the pine family. Because the temple is nestled deep within these trees, it feels almost hidden inside the forest itself. According to historical records, this temple was built in the year 1553 by Raja Bahadur Singh. It is located in an area known as Dungri village, which is why the site is sometimes associated with that name.

This temple is officially recognized by the Government of India as a Monument of National Importance. Under the Ancient Monuments Act of 1967, the government is responsible for its protection, preservation, and maintenance.
You can see ongoing maintenance work around the temple premises. All of this is done to preserve its historical and cultural significance for future generations.

One very unique thing about this temple is that you won’t find traditional idols inside. Instead, it is believed that the footprint of Goddess Hidimba is present here, and that is what devotees worship.
According to mythology, Hidimba was originally considered a demoness. After her marriage to Bhima from the Mahabharata, she was worshipped as a goddess and came to be known as Hidimba Devi.
After her marriage, Hidimba Devi gave birth to a son named Ghatotkacha. There is a separate temple dedicated to him located a short distance from here.
If we look at the architecture of the Hidimba Devi Temple, it has a very distinctive design. The structure features four tiered roofs, with the lower three levels made entirely of wood.
The topmost portion, known as the shikhara or tower, is made of stone. The total height of the temple is approximately 24 meters, making it stand out beautifully among the trees.
Hidimba Devi is believed to be the Protector of the Forest and the Guardian of the Himalayas. This belief adds deep spiritual value to the temple and its surroundings.
The environment here is calm, cool, and incredibly peaceful. There are plenty of seating areas where visitors can relax, meditate, or simply enjoy nature.
The temple becomes quite crowded in the month of May due to a three-day annual festival. Outside of festival season, it’s the perfect place to experience serenity and natural beauty.
Just about 100 to 150 meters from here is the temple of Ghatotkacha. Nearby, you’ll also find museums and a small street market selling traditional Himachali clothing and winter wear.
With that, we come to the end of this video. I hope you enjoyed this peaceful journey through history, culture, and nature. Thank you for watching. See you soon in another video. Bye!
